reading:
Stream Data Centers was founded in 1999. Apollo, the publicly traded alternative asset manager trading as APO, completed a majority acquisition of the company, which now operates as a key platform within the Apollo ecosystem, having formerly been affiliated with Stream Realty Partners.

The company's own site describes more than 27 data center developments delivered across the US, with more than 10 new campuses in development and site selection underway in more than 20 states. Its primary named markets are Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas-Fort Worth, Phoenix, and San Antonio. Apollo's acquisition announcement cites more than 4 gigawatts in active development, with permanent financing backing each project, and Stream states that more than 90 percent of its data center capacity is leased to Fortune 100 customers, with zero early customer terminations across its fully joint-venture project delivery model.

The registry here tracks 3 Stream facilities across two states, Illinois and Texas, a subset of the company's five named primary markets, which also include Atlanta, Phoenix, and San Antonio. Stream's Apollo-backed 4-plus gigawatt active development pipeline is among the larger forward-looking capacity figures recorded in this registry, alongside Aligned's 6.4 gigawatt current-plus-planned total and Vantage's 1.4 gigawatt Texas mega-campus.
